subject: Urgent: Close timeline at risk — MAP and procurement delay
messages:
From: Jamie Torres <jamie@alliedhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@alliedhealth.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Close timeline at risk — MAP and procurement delay

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Quick update from procurement: our internal PO approval slipped — legal finished redlines yesterday but the purchasing team has a queued budget review and they pushed our PO to the next cycle (estimated +3 weeks). That puts our agreed go-live window (week of Mar 21) at risk.

We still want to proceed with Redwood, but timeline slippage means we need to re-evaluate the MAP and any interim steps we can take to avoid missing pilot commitments with our clinical users. Two concrete asks:

- Can Redwood provision a limited canary (single-team pilot) before the formal PO lands? If so, what constraints and cost exposure would that create for Allied?
- In parallel, can we get a short formal re-baseline for the MAP with clear milestones so we can realign internal stakeholders?

I've attached our procurement_summary.pdf which explains the internal cadence and who to chase. Happy to jump on a short call today if helpful.

Thanks,
Jamie Torres
Program Manager, Digital Transformation
Allied Health
---
Attachment: procurement_summary.pdf (2 pages)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie@alliedhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Close timeline at risk — MAP and procurement delay

Jamie — thanks for the heads up and for the doc. Sorry to hear the PO cadence slipped. We can definitely support a short-term plan to keep momentum. A few quick options that we've executed before:

1) Canary pilot: agree to a scoped, time-boxed pilot (team of ~10 users, 2-week window) on developer credits / pilot contract. We can set token and usage caps; Redwood can limit model access to the curated eval subset so production risk is minimal.

2) MAP re-baseline: propose a formal MAP addendum that pushes milestone dates and adds a procurement gating task. We can own the updated milestone tracker and sign off when PO arrives.

3) Contingency credit: for material delays we sometimes offer a one-time service credit tied to milestone acceptance (requires Ops approval). If Allied wants to pursue that, I'll need to loop in Markus for authorization.

I've attached a short MAP draft (Allied_MAP_v3.xlsx) that highlights a possible canary window and re-baselined milestones. Can we schedule a 30-min call today at 2pm PT? If that doesn't work, tomorrow morning also ok.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0128
---
Attachment: Allied_MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Torres <jamie@alliedhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: Close timeline at risk — MAP and procurement delay

Jamie — appreciate the transparency and the procurement summary. Copying Markus to expedite the contingency credit conversation.

Immediate plan (proposal):

1) Canary + Scoped Onboarding (owner: Ben)
   - Window: Mar 14–Mar 27 (2-week pilot + 1 week buffer)
   - Scope: single clinical team, read-only dataset, capped tokens 50k/week
   - Success metrics: 80% reduction in triage time for pilot queries; zero-production-exception incidents
   - Cost: pilot runs on prepaid developer credits with explicit overage protection; estimated exposure $1,500 max

2) MAP Re-baseline Addendum (owner: Lauren + Allied PM)
   - Move Formal Acceptance milestone from Mar 21 -> Apr 12 (+3 weeks)
   - Add procurement gating task: PO approval date and procurement contact; include weekly cadence until PO is in flight
   - Deliverable: updated MAP spreadsheet + sign-off checkbox for each milestone

3) Credit / Escalation Path (owner: Markus)
   - Markus: I can approve a discretionary milestone credit up to $5k tied to acceptance if the PO completes within 30 days of the re-baselined acceptance date. We need Allied to commit to the updated MAP and weekly check-ins.

Next steps:
- Ben: run the canary T&C with Jamie and confirm any legal constraints by EOD today.
- Jamie: confirm whether procurement can fast-track the PO if we split the pilot vs. full contract (i.e., pilot goes on developer-credit path).
- Lauren & Markus: we'll hold a 30-min alignment on Thu Mar 4 10am PT if that works for Allied.

I'll attach a very short runbook for the canary and a template for the MAP addendum this afternoon (runbook will include rollback steps and who to call for incident triage).

We want to preserve momentum while protecting both parties — scope control + clear acceptance criteria is the best way.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0183
---
